candidates.name: Ledger and Margin
candidates.rationale: Debt is a running balance with a known end state (product spec section 1). A ruled household ledger makes every figure traceable to its entry, so provenance and the payoff date read as the closing line of an account the person keeps, not as a score the product awards.
candidates.intended_feel: Calm, orderly and accountable: a well-kept account book on a kitchen table, where nothing is hidden and every correction stays visible.
candidates.form_language: Horizontal rules and a narrow margin column carry structure; figures sit in tabular columns; a red margin rule marks focus and corrections; surfaces are flat paper with no depth effects.
candidates.signature_interaction: Struck-through correction: when a transaction is clarified, the old reading stays visible with a strike and a margin note naming its source, so the change is auditable rather than silently replaced.
candidates.content_behavior: Plain declarative entries in the margin column (source, date, who changed it); the payoff date is written as the closing line of the debt account; no exclamations.
risks: May read as old-fashioned or administrative to younger households (unvalidated).
Dense ruled columns can become cramped on narrow phone screens.
Illustrative control boundary fails the non-text contrast minimum against the paper surface; a darker rule is needed.
accessibility_notes: Tabular figures need programmatic row and column headers so screen readers announce each balance with its account.
The red margin focus rule must be paired with a non-color cue such as a thickened rule for color-vision deficiencies.
Strike-through corrections need a text equivalent, not only a visual strike.

persona_assumptions.text: Households that already keep paper or spreadsheet records will recognise the ledger metaphor.
Seeing a correction history increases trust in categorised transactions rather than causing worry.

feasibility.density: High density suits tabular history; on compact phones the margin column collapses under each row.
feasibility.reduced_motion: Static by nature; strike and margin notes appear without animation, so reduced motion loses nothing.
feasibility.localization_expansion: Margin notes wrap below the entry when translated labels grow; numeric columns stay aligned for Indian digit grouping.
feasibility.android: Maps to Material list and table patterns with custom dividers; no platform-specific identity is required.
feasibility.web: Native tables with sticky headers carry the ledger on wide screens.
feasibility.admin: Ledger rows suit operator queues, but operator views must show metadata only, never user line items.

candidates.name: Route Atlas
candidates.rationale: The product frames a payoff date as a destination rather than a chore (product spec section 1). A route map shows where the household is, the remaining distance and the alternative routes (avalanche, snowball, hybrid) without ranking people.
candidates.intended_feel: Oriented and unhurried: a trip planner open on the table, with the destination fixed and several honest routes to it.
candidates.form_language: A single route line with stations for milestones; contour shading for uncertainty bands; a legend that names every symbol; muted terrain surfaces.
candidates.signature_interaction: Route comparison: switching strategies redraws the route and moves the arrival station, showing time and interest difference side by side instead of a single verdict.
candidates.content_behavior: Wayfinding phrasing such as you are here, remaining distance and arrival estimate; every estimate names its assumptions; missed payments read as a detour, not a failure.
risks: The journey metaphor can imply the product steers the route, close to advice the spec forbids (section 2.3).
Contour shading for uncertainty is faint on the illustrative surface and fails the non-text contrast minimum.
Map literacy varies; the metaphor may confuse some people (unvalidated).
accessibility_notes: Every route and station needs a text summary; the map is never the only carrier of the payoff estimate.
Uncertainty must be stated in words and ranges, not only by shading.
Strategy switching must not rely on drag gestures; plain buttons are required.

persona_assumptions.text: People in repayment respond to a destination framing with less anxiety than to a budget framing.
A detour framing for missed payments avoids shame for people with irregular income.

feasibility.density: Medium; the map needs space, so compact phones show a linear route strip with stations.
feasibility.reduced_motion: Route redraw becomes an instant swap with the changed arrival stated in text.
feasibility.localization_expansion: Station labels sit beside the line and can wrap; the legend grows vertically.
feasibility.android: A custom canvas view for the route strip; standard Material controls for strategy choice.
feasibility.web: A wider route view with the comparison table beside it.
feasibility.admin: Not applicable to operator views beyond a neutral status strip; operators never see user routes.

candidates.name: Almanac Grid
candidates.rationale: Deterministic, verifiable claims are the product's value (product spec section 1). A strict typographic grid with one typeface family lets figures, dates and sources carry the identity, so clarity and provenance are the brand rather than decoration.
candidates.intended_feel: Precise and quiet: a well-set reference timetable where the answer is always in the same place.
candidates.form_language: Asymmetric column grid, strong type hierarchy, flush-left text, black on white with a single signal red; rules instead of boxes; no illustration.
candidates.signature_interaction: Expanding footnote: every figure carries a numbered note that expands in place to show its source, method and uncertainty range.
candidates.content_behavior: Short headline statements followed by figures and footnotes; numbers lead sentences; hedges are explicit ranges, never adjectives.
risks: Can feel cold or clinical at moments of debt anxiety (unvalidated).
Heavy reliance on typography makes the direction sensitive to script coverage beyond Latin.
Close to generic minimal product styling; distinctness depends on disciplined grid and note behavior.
accessibility_notes: Footnote expansion must be keyboard and screen-reader operable with the expanded state announced.
Signal red is reserved for warnings and focus and must always be paired with text or an icon shape.
Type hierarchy must survive user text scaling without overlapping columns.

persona_assumptions.text: People comparing payoff strategies prefer exact figures with sources over reassurance.

feasibility.density: Supports high density on web and admin; compact phones reduce to a single column with footnotes inline.
feasibility.reduced_motion: Footnotes expand without animation; no motion is load-bearing.
feasibility.localization_expansion: Flush-left text tolerates growth; the grid must allow columns to stack when labels expand.
feasibility.android: Fits Material layout grids and typography roles with a constrained palette.
feasibility.admin: Well suited to operator queues and audit views that need dense, scannable metadata.

candidates.name: Cut Paper Household
candidates.rationale: Household debt is a household problem (product spec section 1) and sharing must stay consent-based and revocable (section 2.1). Layered cut paper makes each person's share a separate, removable layer, so what is shared and what is private is physically legible.
candidates.intended_feel: Warm, handmade and human: a family planning sheet made together, where pieces can be added or taken away.
candidates.form_language: Overlapping flat paper shapes with torn or cut edges; each household member has a separate layer; warm pastel surfaces; soft offset edges instead of drop shadows.
candidates.signature_interaction: Lift a layer: revoking a grant lifts that person's layer away at once, and the remaining view shows only what is still shared.
candidates.content_behavior: Warm, second-person language; sharing states are named in full (shared totals only, shared with whom, until revoked); no blame wording for overdue items.
risks: Pastel surfaces fail the non-text contrast minimum for the illustrative control boundary and progress shape, and provenance text fails body-text contrast.
A playful craft look may undercut credibility for large debts (unvalidated).
Layer metaphors can be hard to express to screen-reader users without careful structure.
accessibility_notes: Each layer needs a named region and an explicit owner and scope label.
Control edges need a darker boundary than the illustrative value to meet non-text contrast.
Torn-edge shapes must not obscure text or focus outlines.

persona_assumptions.text: Couples managing shared debt understand separate layers as separate consent.
A warm craft look lowers anxiety without trivialising debt.

feasibility.density: Low density; suits summaries and household views, poor for long transaction lists.
feasibility.reduced_motion: Layer lift becomes an instant removal with a text confirmation of what is no longer shared.
feasibility.localization_expansion: Labels sit on layers that must grow; fixed cut shapes would clip longer translations.
feasibility.android: Custom drawn shapes are feasible but need care to keep Material touch targets and focus visible.
feasibility.web: Layered shapes are feasible with vector drawing; performance on low-end devices needs a check.
feasibility.admin: Not suited to operator tooling; admin would need a separate neutral treatment under the same thesis.

candidates.name: Drafting Table
candidates.rationale: The what-if simulator is instant and deterministic (product spec section 3.2). A technical drawing shows a plan with dimensions, tolerances and revision marks, so a payoff plan reads as an engineered, checkable model and uncertainty is a stated tolerance.
candidates.intended_feel: Competent and transparent: an engineer's plan you can check line by line, with every assumption dimensioned.
candidates.form_language: Fine line work on a deep plan surface, dimension lines for amounts and durations, dashed lines for projected or uncertain values, a title block naming source and revision.
candidates.signature_interaction: Revision block: each change to the plan adds a dated revision row naming what changed and why, and earlier revisions stay viewable.
candidates.content_behavior: Labels in a measured, specification register; projections carry an explicit tolerance; every figure names its basis in the title block.
risks: A dark plan surface may feel technical or intimidating to people new to debt planning (unvalidated).
Dashed uncertainty lines are faint on the illustrative surface and fail the non-text contrast minimum.
Thin line work degrades on low-density screens and in bright outdoor light.
accessibility_notes: Dimensioned values need text equivalents; the drawing is never the only source of a figure.
Dashed lines need a second cue (a label such as projected) because dash patterns are hard to perceive.
A light-surface variant must exist for people who need positive polarity.

persona_assumptions.text: People who use the simulator want to inspect assumptions rather than only see a result.

feasibility.density: High density for plans and schedules; title blocks collapse to a summary row on phones.
feasibility.reduced_motion: Revisions appear as new rows without transitions.
feasibility.localization_expansion: Dimension labels must reflow off the line when translations grow; fixed label boxes would clip.
feasibility.android: Feasible with Material surfaces in a dark scheme plus a required light variant.
feasibility.web: Feasible; vector line work scales on high-density displays.
feasibility.admin: Revision blocks fit audit and change-history views for operators.

candidates.name: Painted Shopfront
candidates.rationale: The product serves households paying in rupees (product spec section 1). Hand-painted shopfront signage is a familiar public language of plain, bold, trustworthy statements; it can make the payoff date and next action unmistakable without banking imagery.
candidates.intended_feel: Direct, local and confident: a clear painted sign that tells you what is here and what to do next.
candidates.form_language: Bold display lettering for one headline figure, flat saturated panels, painted borders around actions, simple pictograms; body text stays in a plain readable face.
candidates.signature_interaction: Next-step panel: one painted panel always names the single next action and its effect on the payoff date; other options sit below in plain text.
candidates.content_behavior: Short imperative headlines and plain sentences; bilingual labels are anticipated; no slang, no hype, no urgency theatre.
risks: Risk of cultural caricature if the signage tradition is used decoratively without local designers (unvalidated).
Display lettering may not cover every Indic script equally well; body text must not use it.
Saturated panels can feel loud during stressful moments.
accessibility_notes: Display lettering is limited to large text; body copy uses a highly legible face.
Saturated yellow surfaces need checks for glare and for people with light sensitivity.
Pictograms always carry visible text labels.

persona_assumptions.text: Households outside metro areas find signage-style statements clearer than app conventions.
A single named next step reduces decision anxiety more than a list of options.

feasibility.density: Low to medium; one headline panel per view, plain lists below.
feasibility.reduced_motion: Static panels; no motion is needed.
feasibility.localization_expansion: Display headlines must shrink or wrap for longer scripts; panels are flexible rectangles.
feasibility.android: Feasible with Material components inside painted panel containers.
feasibility.web: Feasible; display lettering limited to headlines keeps performance acceptable.
feasibility.admin: Operators need a calmer neutral variant; signage panels would overload queue views.

candidates.name: Handloom Weave
candidates.rationale: A household budget is many threads held together: income, debts, goals and members (product spec sections 1 and 3.5). A woven pattern shows each thread separately and the cloth they form together, so shared totals and private details are distinct threads.
candidates.intended_feel: Patient and resilient: cloth built row by row, where a dropped thread is mended rather than hidden.
candidates.form_language: Fine woven textures as quiet backgrounds, coloured threads for each debt or goal, rows of weave as months, indigo and natural cloth surfaces.
candidates.signature_interaction: Row by row: each month adds a woven row; a missed payment shows as a mended thread with its note, not a hole.
candidates.content_behavior: Gentle, steady phrasing; progress is described as rows completed and rows remaining; mending language for setbacks.
risks: Illustrative control boundary and uncertainty threads fail the non-text contrast minimum on the cloth surface.
Textures can reduce text legibility and add visual noise for some readers.
Weaving metaphors may not translate across all audiences (unvalidated).
accessibility_notes: Textures sit behind text only at very low intensity, with a plain-surface option.
Thread colours need distinct patterns or labels so meaning does not rely on colour alone.
Monthly rows need a text table equivalent.

persona_assumptions.text: A mending framing for missed payments supports people with irregular income.

feasibility.density: Medium; the weave suits monthly summaries, while transaction lists use plain rows.
feasibility.reduced_motion: New rows appear without a weaving animation.
feasibility.localization_expansion: Labels sit outside the weave and can wrap freely.
feasibility.android: Feasible with textured surfaces as optional backgrounds behind Material components.
feasibility.web: Feasible; textures must be lightweight and removable.
feasibility.admin: Operators use the plain-surface variant only.
